method: For each of the layer's own polygons, take the platform's returnCentroid point and run it back through a point-in-polygon query against the same layer; record whether the polygon returned is the one the centroid came from.

failures.name: Henrico County
failures.why: Henrico County wraps Richmond City on three sides; the county's centre of mass falls in the hole, which is a different government.

failures.name: Henry County
failures.why: Henry County encloses Martinsville City; same donut shape.

failures.name: Roanoke County
failures.why: Roanoke County encloses Salem City; same donut shape.

failures.name: York County
failures.why: York County is deeply concave around the York River and Poquoson; its centre of mass falls across the water in another county. Not a donut — concavity alone is enough.

conclusion: The design's proposed property test ('every jurisdiction's geometry centroid resolves to itself') is FALSE for Virginia and must not be shipped as written. Virginia's independent cities are excluded from the surrounding county's polygon, so counties that enclose one are topological donuts. A centroid is a label point, never a guaranteed interior point, and is never used here to decide which jurisdiction contains a place.
